games.title: Icewind Dale II
games.note: Brought D&D's third edition rules to the Infinity Engine; Josh Sawyer was lead designer.

games.title: BioShock 2
games.note: Returns to Rapture eight years after the first game, with you playing an early Big Daddy.

games.title: Thief (2014)
games.note: A reboot of the series by Eidos-Montréal, released ten years after Deadly Shadows.

links.took: The Infinity Engine, the frozen Ten-Towns region and combat-focused dungeon crawling.
links.added: D&D 3rd edition rules and a party you build entirely yourself.

links.took: Josh Sawyer, Icewind Dale II's lead designer, who directed Pillars of Eternity.
links.added: Its own world and ruleset instead of licensed D&D rules.

links.took: Rapture, plasmids and the Little Sisters.
links.added: You play a Big Daddy who fights with a plasmid and a weapon at once, plus online multiplayer.

links.took: Garrett, the City and light-and-shadow stealth.
links.added: A reboot with a new story, a 'Focus' vision mode and a hub city.

links.took: The immersive first-person simulation approach of Looking Glass's Underworld.
links.added: A near-future setting, body augmentations and branching choices across real-world locations.

src.t: Wikipedia: Ultima Underworld: The Stygian Abyss

links.extra: Wikipedia lists Deus Ex among games Underworld influenced; Warren Spector worked on both.

links.took: System Shock's cyberpunk look, one of the art team's references.
links.added: A whole open city instead of a single space station.
links.extra: Wikipedia says the art team drew on the first Deus Ex, System Shock and Ghost in the Shell.

links.took: Gothic II's third-person fantasy RPG design; the game was very popular in Poland.
links.added: Geralt, potion alchemy and choices whose consequences appear much later.
links.extra: Wikipedia's Gothic article calls the first two Gothic games a major inspiration for The Witcher series.

links.took: Troika's skill-based character building and reactive quests.
links.added: First-person play on Valve's Source engine in modern Los Angeles.
links.extra: Both were made by Troika Games.
